definitions.explanation: Refers to the very recent past, often to stress that something feels surprisingly recent. The adverb つい means "just (now)" or "only a moment ago."

examples.japanese: つい{昨日|きのう}⟦{会|あ}った→会う：00482_au⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧だ。
つい{昨日|きのう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦のように→のように：30291_noyouni⟧⟦{覚|おぼ}えている→覚える：00739_oboeru⟧。
examples.english: I remember it as if it were just yesterday.

examples.japanese: つい{昨日|きのう}⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧だった⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{急|きゅう}→急：13042_kyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入院|にゅういん}した→入院する：01849_nyuuinsuru⟧。
examples.english: He was perfectly well only yesterday, yet he was suddenly hospitalized.

notes:
つい adds the nuance of "only just," making ⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧ feel very recent or surprisingly close.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- つい{昨日|きのう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧こと⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ようだ: it feels like just yesterday
- ⟦つい{先日|せんじつ}→つい先日：19815_tsuisenjitsu⟧: just the other day (a few days ago)
- ⟦ついさっき→ついさっき：30662_tsuisakki⟧: just a moment ago

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧: yesterday — neutral, without the "only just" nuance
